title: Console: align Usage page with invoice aggregation (timezone normalization + model alias mapping)
author: Chloe Martin
release_notes: Console Usage page now matches invoice aggregation for date boundaries (UTC normalization) and model naming (alias mapping). Adds a small footer note clarifying that invoices are computed in UTC and console can be viewed in local time.
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes two primary sources of mismatch between the Console Usage page and billed totals: (1) time zone / day boundary normalization, and (2) model alias mapping.

The goal is that a customer who sums usage in Console over an invoice period (as shown on the invoice) will match the invoice aggregation within expected tolerances (e.g., retries/outcomes are handled elsewhere; this PR is strictly console display + query alignment).

## Context / why
Finance + Support have flagged recurring confusion where Console totals differ from invoice totals by ~1–6% when customers select a date range that visually matches the invoice period, but Console boundaries were interpreted in the viewer’s local time zone. Additionally, Console previously displayed raw `model_id` in some views while invoice line items group by canonical model aliases / families.

Related tickets: SUP-3112 ("Invoice tokens higher than console"), SUP-3129 (Dedicated commit vs invoice attribution confusion; model naming contributed to confusion).

Related program work: ENG-4825. This is aligned with ADR-027 (rounding/streaming accounting) insofar as we present invoice-aligned windows and naming, but we do not change meter math here.

## Changes
### 1) Time zone normalization
- Usage query windows are now normalized to UTC boundaries before hitting the usage aggregation endpoint.
- The date picker continues to display in the user’s chosen time zone (default: browser), but the backend request uses:
  - `start_utc` = start-of-day (00:00:00) in UTC for the selected start date
  - `end_utc` = end-of-day (23:59:59.999) in UTC for the selected end date
- Added UI copy in the Usage footer: "Invoices are calculated in UTC. This page can be viewed in local time, but totals are computed using UTC day boundaries." (Reviewed w/ Finance wording.)

Why this approach: most customers compare to invoices, which are emitted in UTC windows (billing exports). The previous behavior used local-time boundaries, which is intuitive for daily usage but not for invoice reconciliation. This keeps the UI familiar while aligning totals.

### 2) Model alias mapping
- Added a shared mapping util that resolves `model_id` -> `display_name` (alias) consistent with invoice line items.
- Applies to:
  - the top-level Usage table rows
  - the model filter dropdown
  - CSV export labels
- Mapping is driven by `ModelCatalog.aliases` and falls back to `model_id` when unknown (so new model onboarding doesn’t break the page).
- Added explicit normalization for known historical variants (e.g., `llama-3-70b-instruct` / `llama3-70b-instruct` / region-suffixed ids). This is intentionally minimal and matches what billing uses today.

### 3) “Invoice period” helper
- Added a quick-select for common windows: "This month (UTC)" and "Last month (UTC)".
- This is a small UX addition to reduce support load when customers try to line up periods.

### 4) Tests + instrumentation
- Unit tests for UTC conversion (including DST boundary cases) using fixed TZ fixtures.
- Added a lightweight client-side log event when a user switches timezone display setting (to quantify whether local vs UTC viewing is used).

## Implementation notes
- Frontend: `console/apps/web/src/pages/usage/` now uses a `normalizeDateRangeToUTC()` helper. We intentionally keep all internal state as Date objects, but derive UTC timestamps right before query execution.
- Backend: no aggregation logic changes. This PR only changes request parameters + label mapping.
- CSV export: label changes only; numeric values unchanged.

## QA
Manual QA was done against:
- Finance sample invoice windows (Jan + Feb) using internal test accounts.
- A self-serve account with known high-volume daily traffic (to validate boundaries).
- A Dedicated account view (to ensure model naming isn’t confusing when multiple deployments exist).

Steps:
1) Pick "Last month (UTC)" quick-select.
2) Compare Console total tokens + requests vs invoice line item totals for Hosted API for the same account and period.
3) Repeat with timezone display set to: (a) browser local, (b) UTC.
4) Validate that changing the display timezone does not change totals.
5) Validate model filter shows canonical aliases and selecting a model matches invoice naming.

Observed results:
- Totals now match invoice aggregation for the same UTC invoice window (previously off by ~2–5% depending on the account’s timezone and the selected range).
- Dedicated view unchanged numerically; naming aligns better with invoices and Sales quoting.

### QA screenshots
Attached (internal):
- `usage_utc_quickselect_last_month.png` (shows quick-select and footer note)
- `usage_model_alias_dropdown.png` (shows alias names + fallback behavior)
- `usage_csv_export_headers.png` (shows CSV headers and model label)
- `usage_timezone_toggle_no_total_change.gif` (demonstrates totals unchanged while display tz changes)

## Rollout plan
- Guarded by feature flag: `console.usage.invoice_alignment_v1`
- Rollout:
  1) Enable for Redwood internal orgs + Finance (today)
  2) Enable for 10% of hosted customers tomorrow morning PT
  3) Ramp to 100% after 24h if no increase in "usage page mismatch" support tags and no error rate regressions
- Monitoring:
  - Console page error rate (Sentry + Grafana)
  - Support tag volume for "billing mismatch" (weekly)
  - Internal finance reconciliation spot check for 5 accounts

## Risk / mitigation
- Risk: Some users expect "daily" boundaries to follow their local timezone. Mitigation: keep display in local timezone + clear footer copy; provide explicit UTC quick-selects for invoice matching.
- Risk: Alias mapping could mask raw model_id. Mitigation: hover tooltip shows underlying `model_id`; CSV export includes `model_id` as a separate column (added).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Align Console rounding display to ADR-027 rounding policy (tracked separately; current page shows unrounded token counts per row but totals align).
- After ENG-4823 lands (request outcome/retry dims), consider adding a "Billed tokens" vs "Total tokens" toggle for advanced users.

## Checklist
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [x] Verified no backend meter logic changed
- [x] Finance reviewed copy
- [x] Feature flag + staged rollout

## Links
- Linear: ENG-4825
- Support: SUP-3112, SUP-3129
- ADR reference: ADR-027 (rounding + streaming accounting)

---

## Review conversation (highlights)

**Emily Stone (Finance)**: The footer copy is good, but please avoid implying that viewing in local time changes totals. Can we say "computed using UTC boundaries" explicitly?

**Chloe Martin (author)**: Updated footer to: "Invoices are calculated in UTC. This page can be viewed in local time, but totals are computed using UTC day boundaries." Also added a note to the tooltip on the date range selector.

**Logan Wright (Telemetry/Analytics)**: +1 on UTC normalization. Can we add a unit test that covers DST transitions (e.g., America/Los_Angeles)?

**Chloe Martin (author)**: Added DST fixtures and tests in `usageDateRange.test.ts` for both spring-forward and fall-back.

**Nadia Rahman (Metering pipelines)**: Model alias mapping: please ensure this matches billing’s canonicalization logic (region suffix handling). Is the mapping table sourced from the same catalog?

**Chloe Martin (author)**: Yes—using `ModelCatalog.aliases` which is the same source consumed by billing export. I only added a small compatibility normalization for a couple of historical ids we still see in telemetry.

**Allison Grant (Observability)**: Rollout flag looks fine. Please add a dashboard link / note for oncall if this increases console errors.

**Chloe Martin (author)**: Added a comment in the rollout section and linked the Console Web error dashboard in the runbook (internal link in PR description).

**Cole Summers (Billing hooks)**: CSV change: including `model_id` separately is helpful. Confirm this doesn’t break downstream users of the export.

**Chloe Martin (author)**: The existing columns are unchanged; we only append `model_id` at the end. Also updated the CSV schema doc string in code.

Approvals:
- Emily Stone: Approved
- Logan Wright: Approved
- Nadia Rahman: Approved
- Allison Grant: Approved
